items.title: AI 展望：OpenAI 削減籌款目標，Meta 收到現金流和支出信用警告
items.originalTitle: AI outlook: OpenAI cuts fundraising goal while Meta gets a credit warning on cash flow and spending
items.originalSummary: OpenAI , the company behind ChatGPT, has lowered its fundraising target from $30 billion to $20 billion, indicating potential financial challenges amid a broader slowdown in AI investment. This adjustment comes as rival Anthropic ’s possible listing complicates the fundraising landscape. Concurrently, Meta Platforms has received a credit warning from S&P Global Ratings, which has revised its outlook to negative due to concerns over high spending, cash flow deficits, and uncertainties surrounding AI monetization. These developments suggest increased financial scrutiny and potential reevaluation of AI-focused business strategies. Observers will be keen on OpenAI’s next moves regarding its fundraising efforts and whether it successfully secures necessary capital amidst market pressures. Meta’s financial performance and strategic adjustments in AI monetization will be critical in addressing S&P’s concerns. Both companies’ actions could influence broader market sentiment toward AI investments, particularly if they announce significant strategic shifts or encounter further financial obstacles.

items.originalTitle: Google's AI satellite sends a very expensive haiku to Earth
items.originalSummary: Google’s AI chip-equipped satellite has generated its first response from space. In a blog post on Friday, Google says it successfully booted up the satellite’s Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), allowing the on-board Gemma 4 model to follow through on a prompt to create a haiku about being in space: > Blue marble below > Data streams in silent grace > Starlight feeds my core. ✨ Google says it tried out other space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts as well. The test is part of Google’s Project Suncatcher, an experimental initiative that could eventually put AI data centers in space. Google launched the satellite into orbit earlier this month. [Media: https://twitter.com/sundarpichai/status/2116214866444943853?a=G1C1xOJ0uzlQ1Fp1q50&s=20] “Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit,” Google says. “Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027.”

items.originalTitle: Google's Space Satellite Runs AI In Orbit For The First Time, Writes A Poem And Sends It Back To Earth
items.originalSummary: Google's ambitious Project Suncatcher has taken a major leap forward. The tech giant's prototype satellite, launched earlier this month, has successfully generated its first AI-powered response. The achievement marks an important milestone in the exploration of artificial intelligence (AI) technology in space. The response was a haiku about life in orbit and was generated by a data center-class Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) operating in space for the first time. The prototype satellite, which was launched on October 1, successfully powered up its TPU and creatively generated a haiku about the cosmos. The poem read: Blue marble below / Data streams in silent grace / Starlight feeds my core. Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced this development on X, calling it a hello world milestone for Project Suncatcher. The next phase of Project Suncatcher will involve testing the TPUs under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit. These tests are crucial to determine if the chips can reliably run computing workloads in space. If successful, Google plans to take another big step by launching two interconnected satellites in 2027. This could pave the way for larger AI workloads handled by satellite constellations. Project Suncatcher is a long-term research effort by Google to explore whether space could support scalable machine learning (ML) infrastructure. The company is looking into the possibility of connecting satellite groups to handle larger AI workloads. If successful, this could revolutionize how we think about and use artificial intelligence in our daily lives.

items.originalTitle: Google Achieves Major Milestone In Space-Based AI Computing As Satellite Sends First AI-Generated Response To Earth
items.originalSummary: Google has successfully received the first artificial intelligence response from a data centre-class processor operating in orbit, marking a significant milestone for its Project Suncatcher initiative. The prototype satellite, which launched on 1 October aboard a SpaceX rocket, transmitted an AI-generated haiku back to Earth after completing its initial commissioning phase. During a ground-station pass, engineers sent a prompt to the satellite's onboard Gemma 4 model, asking it to write a haiku about being in space. The satellite's Tensor Processing Unit processed the request and transmitted the response as it passed over Svalbard, Norway. Google CEO Sundar Pichai described the achievement as a "hello world" milestone for the project, which aims to explore whether AI computing infrastructure can operate reliably in space. The satellite carries four TPUs designed to test whether Google's AI hardware can withstand the harsh conditions of orbit, including radiation exposure and extreme temperatures. Over the past few weeks, the team has been powering up the hardware trays and running early machine learning tests to verify the system's functionality in the space environment. Project Suncatcher represents Google's long-term research effort to determine whether space could support scalable machine learning infrastructure. The company envisions solar-powered satellite constellations that could handle AI workloads while bypassing the energy and physical constraints facing terrestrial data centres. The successful response provides crucial proof that data centre-class TPU hardware can execute machine learning tasks in orbit and communicate results back to Earth. Google plans to progress to its next milestone: deploying two interconnected satellites in 2027. These tests will help determine whether the company's AI chips can reliably handle computing workloads in the challenging space environment, potentially paving the way for larger satellite constellations capable of processing more complex AI tasks. items.originalTitle: Google's AI model achieves a milestone with first response from space in Project Suncatcher
items.originalSummary: New Delhi [India], October 31 (ANI): Google has successfully run an artificial intelligence (AI) model on a satellite in orbit and received its first complete response back on Earth, marking a key milestone in its Project Suncatcher initiative to explore the possibility of running AI computing infrastructure in space. Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced the development in a post on X, describing it as a “‘hello world’ milestone for Project Suncatcher”. He said the team had sent a command to the satellite, booted up its Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), run a prompt and received the response back on Earth. “After launching our prototype satellite a few weeks ago, we’ve now successfully sent a command up to orbit, booted up the TPU, ran the prompt, and received our first complete response back on earth - a haiku!” Pichai said. According to a blog post by Google, the prototype satellite was launched on October 1 as part of the company's long-term research effort to examine whether space could support scalable machine learning infrastructure. The company said the satellite completed its initial commissioning checks over the following weeks, including powering up its host and TPU trays and running early machine learning tests. During a ground-station pass, the team sent a prompt to the onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about space. The response was received as the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway. Google said it subsequently tested the system with space-themed limericks and prompts asking it to report the technical status of the satellite's systems. The next phase will involve testing how the TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit. These tests are intended to establish whether the chips can reliably run computing workloads in the space environment. The company said successful testing would pave the way for its next milestone: two interconnected satellites in 2027. Project Suncatcher is exploring whether satellites could eventually be linked into constellations to handle larger AI workloads. Google has said satellites in low Earth orbit could access near-constant sunlight and potentially generate up to eight times more solar power than on Earth. The latest milestone follows Google's announcement of the project, when it said the initial satellite mission would test whether its TPUs could survive and operate in space. (ANI)

items.originalTitle: Google Tests AI in Space, Receives First TPU-Generated Response
items.originalSummary: Google has achieved a significant milestone in its efforts to explore artificial intelligence (AI) computing in space. The company has successfully received its first AI-generated response from a data centre-class Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) operating aboard a satellite in orbit.Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced the development on X (formerly Twitter), describing it as a “hello world” milestone for Project Suncatcher.“After launching our prototype satellite a few weeks ago, we've now successfully sent a command up to orbit, booted up the TPU, ran the prompt, and received our first complete response back on earth - a haiku!” Pichai wrote..Google Receives First AI Response from Space.The milestone marks the first successful AI response generated by a data centre-class TPU in orbit. According to Google, the team sent its first prompt to the onboard Gemma 4 open model during a ground-station pass, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space.As the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway, the team received the poem back on Earth, confirming that the test was successful.The AI-generated haiku read:“Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core.”Following the initial response, Google also tested the system with space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts designed to report the technical status of the satellite's onboard systems..What is Google's Project Suncatcher?.Google launched its prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher on October 1. The launch marked the first step in the company's long-term research initiative to explore the possibility of powering AI computing infrastructure in space.Over the following weeks, engineers completed commissioning checks, powered up the host and TPU trays, and successfully conducted early machine learning tests.Project Suncatcher aims to explore AI data centres in space using networks of solar-powered satellites equipped with Google's custom TPUs. The idea is to use the Sun's energy to power computing operations in orbit, potentially reducing the need for land and electricity resources on Earth.Also Read: Google Home Update Adds Matter Controls and Energy Monitoring.Google Plans More Satellite Tests in 2027.The next phase will involve testing how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit. Google will assess whether its chips can reliably execute computing workloads in space.Successful testing would pave the way for the company's next milestone: launching two interconnected satellites in 2027..Join our WhatsApp Channel to get the latest news, exclusives and videos on WhatsApp

He said the team had sent a command to the satellite, booted up its Tensor Processing Unit (TPU), run a prompt and received the response back on Earth."After launching our prototype satellite a few weeks ago, we've now successfully sent a command up to orbit, booted up the TPU, ran the prompt, and received our first complete response back on earth - a haiku!" Pichai said.According to a blog post by Google, the prototype satellite was launched on October 1 as part of the company's long-term research effort to examine whether space could support scalable machine learning infrastructure.The company said the satellite completed its initial commissioning checks over the following weeks, including powering up its host and TPU trays and running early machine learning tests.During a ground-station pass, the team sent a prompt to the onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about space. The response was received as the satellite passed over Svalbard, Norway.Google said it subsequently tested the system with space-themed limericks and prompts asking it to report the technical status of the satellite's systems.The next phase will involve testing how the TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit. These tests are intended to establish whether the chips can reliably run computing workloads in the space environment.The company said successful testing would pave the way for its next milestone: two interconnected satellites in 2027.Project Suncatcher is exploring whether satellites could eventually be linked into constellations to handle larger AI workloads. Google has said satellites in low Earth orbit could access near-constant sunlight and potentially generate up to eight times more solar power than on Earth.The latest milestone follows Google's announcement of the project, when it said the initial satellite mission would test whether its TPUs could survive and operate in space.(Except for the headline, this story has not been edited by NDTV staff and is published from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: 谷歌剛剛讓人工智慧在太空中進行對話——Suncatcher 計畫在 SpaceX 發射後首次在軌 TPU 回應
items.originalTitle: Google Just Got AI To Talk From Space — Project Suncatcher Scores First In-Orbit TPU Response After SpaceX Launch
items.originalSummary: Google said on October 30, 2026, that its Project Suncatcher prototype satellite returned its first AI response from orbit: a haiku generated by an onboard Gemma 4 open model running on a data-center-class Tensor Processing Unit (TPU). Travis Beals, Senior Director of Paradigms of Intelligence at Google, announced the milestone in a Google Research post , describing it as the mission’s “Hello World” milestone and what the company characterized as the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit. During a ground-station pass, the team uplinked its first prompt to the satellite’s onboard Gemma 4 model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space. As the satellite passed Svalbard, Norway, the downlinked poem confirmed success: “Blue marble below / Data streams in silent grace / Starlight feeds my core.” Following the initial output, the team tested space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts that reported the technical status of the payload systems. The satellite launched on October 1, 2026, aboard the Transporter-18 rideshare mission with SpaceX and was built in partnership with Planet, according to Google’s launch announcement. The team confirmed contact with the spacecraft and said it was operating as expected. In the weeks after launch, the team completed a commissioning checklist that included powering up the host and TPU trays and successfully running early machine learning tests, Beals wrote. The mission is designed to gather in-orbit data on how Google’s TPUs handle the physical stress of spaceflight and the radiation and thermal extremes of space, according to the launch announcement. A peer-reviewed paper detailing the research behind the mission is now available in the journal Joule. Google announced Project Suncatcher on November 4, 2025, describing it as a long-term research moonshot exploring whether an interconnected network of solar-powered satellites equipped with its TPU AI chips could one day scale machine learning in space. The company’s initial research, shared in a preprint paper alongside the announcement, described its approach to satellite constellation design, control, and communication, along with initial learnings from radiation testing of Google TPUs. The plan then called for a learning mission in partnership with Planet to launch two prototype satellites by early 2027 to test the hardware in orbit. In a behind-the-scenes engineering post published September 24, 2026, Google said that in low Earth orbit, satellites can access near-constant sunlight, generating up to eight times more solar power than on Earth. The company said it could eventually be possible to link together multiple constellations of satellites, allowing them to manage larger AI workloads while in orbit. Before the launch, the team tested whether the hardware could survive the trip to orbit. A rocket ride into low Earth orbit lasts about 10 minutes, with sustained acceleration loads up to 10 times the force of gravity, and individual components such as the TPU chips can experience forces of 50 to 100 g, according to the engineering post. The team conducted vibration testing by intensely shaking the satellite on all three axes

items.title: 特斯拉取消在澳洲和紐西蘭推出 Cyber​​truck
items.originalTitle: Tesla cancels Cybertruck launch in Australia and New Zealand
items.originalSummary: Tesla has cancelled plans to sell its polarising Cybertruck in Australia and New Zealand, after hopeful locals who paid deposits to secure the electric ute spent years waiting for news of its arrival. The Elon Musk-led company began contacting affected customers last week, informing them that their reservations had been cancelled and their $150 deposits would be returned. A Tesla spokesperson would not confirm why the EV-maker decided to ditch the Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand, but said the firm had made the decision following "careful consideration". "We understand this will be disappointing for many, and we appreciate our customers' understanding," they told Information Age . "We remain focused on the road ahead for Tesla in Australia and New Zealand, including Full Self-Driving (Supervised) and the recently launched Model 3 Rear-Wheel Drive." Customers who made reservations for Cybertrucks would be contacted directly, with full refunds of any remaining deposits to be processed "within 30 days of confirmation", they added. "We thank these customers for their early support," they said. "Customers with a cancelled reservation will be offered a complimentary one-year Full Self-Driving (Supervised) subscription when they order a new Model 3 or Model Y, applied after delivery." An Australian reservation page was reportedly removed from Tesla's website in mid-2022, but deposits were not automatically refunded. Tesla had even shown off the Cybertruck at several Australian automotive roadshows in recent years, where the company also signed up prospective buyers to receive alerts about potential future availability.

historyItems.title: FORM 與 COHU：哪種半導體測試股票比較值得買？
historyItems.summary: FormFactor FORM 和 Cohu COHU 是半導體測試設備提供商，受益於人工智慧 (AI) 基礎設施投資的加速、半導體複雜性的增加、對高頻寬記憶體 (HBM) 的需求不斷增長以及先進封裝技術的廣泛採用。然而，他們的核心產品差異很大。 FormFactor 專注於先進晶圓級探針卡、MEMS 技術和光子測試解決方案，為代工廠、邏輯和記憶體製造商提供服務。相較之下，Cohu 專注於高效能處理器和功率元件的自動化測試處理器、先進熱管理、半導體偵測、測試介面和自動化測試設備。
historyItems.originalTitle: FORM vs. COHU: Which Semiconductor Testing Stock is a Better Buy?
historyItems.originalSummary: FormFactor FORM and Cohu COHU are semiconductor testing equipment providers benefiting from accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments, increasing semiconductor complexity, growing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and expanding adoption of advanced packaging technologies. However, their core offerings differ significantly. FormFactor specializes in advanced wafer-level probe cards, MEMS technologies and photonics testing solutions, serving foundry, logic and memory manufacturers. In contrast, Cohu focuses on automated test handlers, advanced thermal management, semiconductor inspection, test interfaces and automated test equipment for high-performance processors and power devices. FORM or COHU, which is a better buy currently?

historyItems.originalTitle: Intel Plunges After PC Slump and Supply Snags Hurt Outlook
historyItems.originalSummary: [SAN FRANCISCO] Intel plunged in late trading after its revenue forecast missed analysts’ estimates, hurt by sputtering demand for PC processors and supply chain problems with its lucrative data centre components. Sales in the fourth quarter will be US$15 billion to US$16 billion, the company said on Thursday (Oct 29) in a statement. Analysts, on average, estimated US$17 billion and some projections topped US$18 billion, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Profit will be US$0.25 a share in the quarter, excluding certain items. Wall Street was projecting adjusted earnings of US$0.43 a share.

historyItems.originalTitle: Learn Why The Bull Case For Micron Stock Could Change Following Memory Shortage Warning
historyItems.originalSummary: Micron Technology is in focus after SK Hynix reported record quarterly results and projected tight memory supply through 2030, while Micron continued to secure long term customer agreements and maintained its regular US$0.15 cash dividend that went ex dividend on 14 October 2026. The same supply constraints that SK Hynix links to AI and data center demand are feeding into Micron's DRAM, HBM and NAND roadmap. Management is preparing to discuss technology leadership and capacity planning that tie directly to its long term supply agreements. We will now look at how Micron Technology's AI driven memory tightness, signalled by SK Hynix, could reshape the overall investment narrative.

historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne (TER) Dropped, So What Is Behind The Latest Attention?
historyItems.originalSummary: Teradyne (TER) just posted third quarter 2026 results that surprised the market, with revenue of US$1.31b and net income of US$342.4 million. However, the stock dropped after the release. Teradyne's shares fell 3.23% on the day of the release and are down 22.28% over the past month. However, the year-to-date share price return of 50.92% and 1-year total shareholder return of 77.43% indicate that longer term momentum remains strong despite this pullback.

historyItems.originalTitle: Hackers Exploited Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Plant Malware Built to Steal Encryption Keys
historyItems.originalSummary: PHP2Shell security flaws now sucessfully exploited in the wild DreamHost forces password resets in ongoing "incident" Kali Linux 2026.3 released with 6 new tools, desktop updates Critical 'HTTP2Shell' Brotli vulnerability triggers emergency patches How to access the Dark Web using the Tor Browser How to enable Kernel-mode Hardware-enforced Stack Protection in Windows 11 How to backup and restore the Windows Registry A newly identified advanced persistent threat (APT) group tracked as UAT-11473 was observed exploiting CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers, to deploy a custom malware framework called KeyDrift. CVE-2026-20127 is a max-severity flaw that Cisco patched in February 2026, which allows remote attackers to gain privileged access to Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager and add rogue peers. UAT-8616 has exploited the vulnerability as a zero-day since at least 2023 , and recent research also linked its exploitation to the Chinese Volt Typhoon state-sponsored hacking group.

historyItems.title: SpaceX 供應商意法半導體預測人工智慧和衛星將帶來強勁銷售
historyItems.summary: 作者：Mauro Orru 意法半導體預計今年的銷售將強勁增長，因為為人工智慧模型提供支援的資料中心的建設以及提供連接服務的衛星的部署刺激了對半導體的需求。這家歐洲晶片製造商的客戶包括蘋果和馬斯克旗下的特斯拉和 SpaceX，該公司表示，2026 年營收預計將年增近 23%，達到約 145 億美元。同時，其毛利率（一項受到密切關注的定價能力指標）應會從去年的 33.9% 增加到 36.4% 左右。直到現在，該公司一直沒有提供詳細的年度指引，因為該公司即將進入最後一個季度，以便更好地了解推動需求的因素。
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Supplier STMicroelectronics Forecasts Strong Sales on AI, Satellite Boost
historyItems.originalSummary: By Mauro Orru STMicroelectronics projected robust sales growth for the year as the build-out of data centers to power artificial-intelligence models and the deployment of satellites to provide connectivity services fuel demand for semiconductors. The European chip maker, which counts Apple and Elon Musk's Tesla and SpaceX among its clients, said 2026 revenue should grow nearly 23% on year to roughly $14.5 billion. Meanwhile, its gross margin--a closely watched measure of pricing power--should increase to about 36.4% from 33.9% last year. The company had refrained from providing detailed annual guidance until now , as it embarks on the final quarter, gaining better visibility into what is driving demand. It expects sales of about $4.15 billion this quarter compared with $3.33 billion a year earlier, above a Visible Alpha forecast of nearly $4.12 billion. Its annual sales projection is also above a Visible Alpha forecast of $14.41 billion. Chief Executive Jean-Marc Chery singled out data centers and satellites as key drivers for growth this year. Like other chip makers, STMicroelectronics is reaping the benefits of hundreds of billions of dollars in spending commitments from some of the world's largest tech groups to build out AI infrastructure. STMicroelectronics stock has nearly doubled in value since the year began, riding a wave of investor fervor around AI that lifted global semiconductor stocks. In a sign of how fast demand for chips to power energy-intensive data centers is building up, STMicroelectronics in July projected revenue from data centers above $1 billion in 2026 and well above $2 billion in 2027 compared with prior guidance of about $1 billion and roughly $2 billion, respectively. That marked the second time the company raised its AI forecasts this year. Alongside data centers, space also provides a key revenue stream for STMicroelectronics and other chip makers that supply semiconductors for low-Earth-orbit satellite constellations. The company expects well above $3 billion in revenue between 2026 and 2028 for the supply of equipment to be used in space, a forecast that for now excludes potential benefits from orbital data centers. Low Earth-orbit satellite networks are closer to Earth than traditional constellations, making them ideal to beam low-latency broadband directly to smartphones in parts of the world where cell towers are unavailable. SpaceX's Starlink provides direct-to-device connectivity to users in several countries, including Ukraine, where damage to terrestrial networks because of the war is common. STMicroelectronics had long relied on the automotive industry to generate a significant portion of its sales. Data centers and satellites have allowed the group to diversify its revenue streams and become less tied to carmakers. The auto industry in recent years had slowly been digesting chip inventories it built at the height of the pandemic, weighing on demand for new orders in a blow to STMicroelectronics. historyItems.originalTitle: Nvidia Partner Vertiv Soars After Blowout Earnings, Strong Guidance
historyItems.originalSummary: The stock of the data center infrastructure company Vertiv Holdings (NYSE: VRT) experienced a powerful rally in the extended session leading toward the Wednesday, October 28, morning bell, rising 16.13% from $208.56 at the latest close to $242.20 at press time. This move came as a continuation of the 9% recovery that started late last week, which left VRT shares 3.50% in the red on the weekly chart and 14.54% down on the monthly chart. Still, the pre-market move helped erase all losses suffered since October 9. Vertiv stock’s latest upsurge came as a result of a particularly impressive earnings report that showed the company beat Wall Street forecasts in terms of both revenue and earnings-per-share (EPS).

historyItems.originalTitle: AI Data Center Supplier Amphenol Jumps On Earnings Beat
historyItems.originalSummary: Burke Wealth Management, an investment management company, released its "Focused Growth Strategy" Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here . The fund delivered strong results in the third quarter of 2026, benefiting from a sharp recovery in enterprise software and solid corporate earnings amid continued market volatility. The composite returned 10.8% net of fees, substantially outperforming the S&P 500 Total Return Index's 2.3% gain, while its year-to-date return reached 20.0%, compared with 12.7% for the benchmark. The firm attributed the quarter's strength partly to investors reassessing the long-term value of enterprise software platforms that can securely connect AI models with proprietary business data. Burke believes these platforms can serve as essential AI "harnesses," providing permissions, security, and context for enterprise applications, although it cautions that AI agents could challenge traditional software business models and seat-based pricing. Looking ahead, Burke remains optimistic about the remainder of 2026, citing strong corporate earnings growth and the transition from AI infrastructure investment toward practical applications that may improve productivity and consumer experiences. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

historyItems.originalTitle: Oracle Jumps After Projecting Return to Positive Cash Flow
historyItems.originalSummary: Oracle projected its long-term financial guidance presented at its annual investor conference in Las Vegas. (From Profits Run) Key Points GE Vernova beat third-quarter revenue and earnings estimates and raised its 2026 outlook, yet shares still fell about 2% on the news. Firm gas turbine backlog rose to 64 gigawatts as more slot reservations converted into signed orders, though new contract signings slowed sharply from the prior quarter. Power segment margins and orders surged while Wind losses widened and Electrification orders dipped. Special Report : See How You Could Qualify for the Fastest Second Citizenship as an American Today (From International Living) GE Vernova (NYSE: GEV) gave investors plenty to like in its third-quarter report , released before the open on Wednesday, Oct. 28. Revenue climbed 27% to $12.6 billion, comfortably ahead of the roughly $12 billion analysts expected, and earnings of $4.81 per share beat the $4.03 consensus. Orders nearly doubled on an organic basis to $29.3 billion, while total backlog grew by $20 billion in a single quarter to $197 billion. Management also raised its 2026 outlook for revenue, margins, and free cash flow, and doubled its share repurchase authorization to $20 billion. Still, the stock slid as much as 6.6% intraday before closing down about 2% for the day, leaving it 27% below its 52-week high. That reaction says a lot. With AI infrastructure stocks under pressure, a bigger backlog alone no longer impresses the market. The more important question is what that backlog is actually made of, and how much of it is turning into firm business. Larry Benedict, who ran a $900 million hedge fund and posted 20 consecutive years without a loss, including over $274 million in audited net income between 2004 and 2012, says one long forgotten American company already holds what Musk needs. Firm backlog consists of signed equipment orders. Slot reservation agreements hold a customer’s place in the production line, but they aren’t orders yet. As of June 30, the company had 53 GW of firm backlog and 63 GW of slot reservations. In the third quarter, it converted 13 GW of reservations into firm orders, up from 10 GW the prior quarter, while shipping 5 GW of equipment. That pushed firm backlog up to 64 GW and brought reservations down to 58 GW, for 122 GW under contract in total. Notably, that’s the shift management pointed to last quarter , with firm orders now outweighing reservations. The company also raised its year-end goal to at least 130 GW under contract, up from 125 GW. historyItems.originalSummary: Fred Alger Management , an investment management company, released its "Alger Spectra Fund" third-quarter 2026 investor letter. The letter can be downloaded here . During the third quarter of 2026, U.S. equities delivered modest gains, with the S&P 500 advancing 2%. Despite robust corporate earnings and resilient consumer spending, market breadth remained weak as 60% of S&P 500 constituents closed lower. Against this backdrop, the fund lagged the Russell 3000 Growth Index. Class A shares of the fund returned 0.29% without a sales charge and -4.98% with sales charges, compared to 0.45% for the index. Consumer Discretionary and Tech drove the relative performance, whereas Communication Services and Utilities dragged. Macro headwinds weighed on sectors like Energy following oil supply disruptions. On the short side, a position in an IT consulting firm detracted from returns, while a short in an advertising technology company generated positive gains following its weak earnings report and rising competitive threats. Amid these shifting dynamics, the fund continues to prioritize disciplined stock selection to capture long-term opportunities across the expanding AI ecosystem. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

historyItems.originalTitle: Secure keys strengthen protected military satellite communications
historyItems.originalSummary: At any given moment, a U.S. Air Force pilot may be maneuvering an aircraft mid-mission, a U.S. Navy officer resurfacing a submarine after weeks undersea, or a U.S. Army technician offloading drone data in a combat zone. Each operation depends on satellite communications (satcom) and, specifically, on cryptographic keys that allow terminals to communicate securely while keeping adversaries locked out. At the scale of modern operations, managing these keys is a technical challenge. Every terminal needs to have the right keys at the right time, quickly and securely, and if any keys are compromised, they need to be refreshed without leaving out devices that may be offline, disconnected, or under attack. MIT Lincoln Laboratory researchers have now solved this challenge with the Protected Anti-Jam Tactical Satcom (PATS) Key Management System (KMS) Prototype. This new architecture enables keys to refresh rapidly across terminals dispersed worldwide, even in contested or bandwidth-constrained environments. "We're enabling the nation to achieve highly assured, highly available communications. Even when adversaries know where forces are operating and are trying to stop them from communicating, they're unable to do so, because we've built in smarts across this entire system to keep talking," says Joseph Sobchuk, a principal investigator of the PATS KMS Prototype program and researcher in the Secure Resilient Systems and Technology Group . This architecture is being adopted as the cryptographic backbone of the U.S. Space Force's next-generation satcom system, PATS. The KMS Prototype serves as the gold-standard reference implementation for the industry-built operational KMS, which will be integrated across the PATS ecosystem, encompassing satellites, user terminals on military platforms, and ground-based communication hubs. Developed under sponsorship of the Space Force's Space Systems Command (SSC), the KMS Prototype reflects Lincoln Laboratory's end-to-end approach to technology development, from shaping the core key-management concepts to putting them into practice in a prototype to transitioning a technical baseline to government and industry. For this transitioned innovation, the SSC and Lincoln Laboratory team received a 2025 R&D 100 Award , recognizing the KMS Prototype among the year's most impactful new technologies. Cryptographic keys are foundational to secure communications. These keys, strings of random characters used by cryptographic algorithms, help protect communications by encrypting data and supporting protected transmission patterns, such as frequency hopping . Without key protection, the communications sent and received by terminals are more susceptible to eavesdropping and interference. Historically, operators manually uploaded keys to terminals before missions. More recently, some systems have supported over-the-air key updates, but bandwidth constraints, security concerns, and operational complexity have limited real-time, wide-scale refresh. historyItems.originalTitle: Snowflake and Oracle Expand Their Partnership to Bring the Snowflake AI Data Cloud to OCI
historyItems.originalSummary: New first-party service gives customers more choice and flexibility to accelerate enterprise AI initiatives and realize business value faster LAS VEGAS, Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oracle AI World -- Oracle and Snowflake (NYSE: SNOW) today announced that Snowflake AI Data Cloud will be available as a native, first-party service on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), further expanding the AI and data capabilities Oracle offers to help organizations accelerate enterprise AI initiatives. By making Snowflake available alongside Oracle's comprehensive portfolio of infrastructure, AI, data, and application services, Oracle will give customers greater flexibility to put their enterprise data to work and drive AI-powered innovation. Customers will be able to purchase and provision the offering directly through Oracle, with simplified pricing and billing, alongside the ability to use Oracle Universal Credits.

historyItems.originalTitle: Google and Oracle are partnering to bring Google TPUs to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
historyItems.originalSummary: OCI will be the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer Google TPUsLAS VEGAS, Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Oracle AI World -- Oracle and Google today announced that Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) will be available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), marking the first time Google TPUs will be offered on a hyperscale cloud platform outside Google. By bringing Google's purpose-built TPUs to OCI's AI compute portfolio, customers gain the flexibility to match their most demanding workloads with infrastructure designed for near-linear scalability and highly optimized economics. "Different AI workloads have different compute needs," said Mahesh Thiagarajan, president, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle. "Bringing Google TPUs to OCI gives customers access to multiple leading AI compute architectures in one cloud. That choice gives them the flexibility to choose the right infrastructure for the performance, throughput, and economics of each AI workload."Google TPUs are custom accelerators co-designed with open software to power the entire AI lifecycle—from frontier training and large-scale inference to the multi-step reasoning data demands of agentic AI. OCI will provide the power, cooling, and datacenter networking to deploy Google TPUs at scale within its infrastructure."The next generation of AI will require a diverse range of compute," said Amin Vahdat, senior vice president and chief technologist, AI & Infrastructure, Google. "TPUs give customers a powerful, purpose-built option for demanding training and inference workloads. Bringing Google TPUs to OCI will give more organizations access to this technology and greater flexibility in how they build and run their most complex AI applications."More AI Compute Options for Every WorkloadAs models grow and production inference demands increase, the performance and economics of every training run and inference request become increasingly important. Google's TPU architecture is designed to maximize AI processing from each watt of electricity, with fast access to model data and rapid communication between chips.Google TPUs can support large-model training and post-training, including dense and mixture-of-experts models (MoE), as well as production inference for reasoning, agentic, and long-context applications. Customers will be able to choose Google TPUs within OCI, optimized for their workloads, performance requirements, and cost objectives.Drawing on more than a decade of custom AI silicon development, Google's TPU portfolio delivers purpose-built compute optimized for massive machine learning workloads. Google's eighth-generation TPU introduces two purpose-built architectures: TPU 8t for training and TPU 8i for inference. TPU 8t cuts frontier model development cycles from months to weeks, delivering nearly 3x the compute performance per pod over the previous generation, while TPU 8i is designed to handle the iterative work of many specialized agents.Google TPUs on OCI will be available in calendar year 2027, ramping over a multi-year period to meet customer needs.Additional ResourcesLearn more about Oracle C

historyItems.originalTitle: OpenAI expands partnership with Oracle to bring its apps to ChatGPT
historyItems.originalSummary: OpenAI said it is expanding its partnership with Oracle to bring business applications and AI agents into ChatGPT, while also helping power new Oracle offerings, according to an OpenAI announcement published on Oct. 27, 2026. The update extends a relationship that has already moved beyond infrastructure and into enterprise distribution. In its announcement, OpenAI said the companies are working to place Oracle business applications and AI agents inside ChatGPT, and to support new Oracle products through the collaboration. The statement did not include pricing, rollout timing, customer counts or a product launch schedule. The partnership has been building through multiple prior steps. OpenAI said on Aug. 7, 2026 that eligible Oracle Universal Credits can be used to purchase OpenAI API models, Codex and ChatGPT Work through Oracle Marketplace. Oracle also said on Oct. 16, 2026 that its own employees were adopting Enterprise ChatGPT as part of its AI-transformation update, indicating internal use of OpenAI software within the company. The expansion comes against a broader backdrop of joint infrastructure development. Oracle said in a June 11, 2024 announcement with Microsoft and OpenAI that Oracle Cloud Infrastructure would supply additional capacity by extending Microsoft’s Azure AI platform. OpenAI later named Oracle among the initial equity funders in its Jan. 21, 2025 Stargate announcement, which outlined an intention to invest $500 billion in U.S. AI infrastructure over four years. OpenAI then said on July 22, 2025 that it had agreed with Oracle to develop an additional 4.5 gigawatts of U.S. Stargate capacity, taking the total described in that update to more than 5 gigawatts under development and more than 2 million chips. Those figures described planned development, not already completed capacity. Oracle’s current infrastructure page, as of September 2026, said Abilene had delivered 75% of total capacity, while customer delivery at Shackelford and Doña Ana County was scheduled to begin in the first half of 2027. That timeline gives the partnership a physical infrastructure layer, while the new OpenAI announcement points to a broader software and distribution tie-up. There were no verified details in the source material on financial terms, revenue impact, exclusivity, or an official launch date for the new ChatGPT integrations. The timing of any further product rollout remains unknown from the supplied material.

historyItems.originalTitle: Market Rotation Overshadows KLA Corp’s (KLAC) Solid Results and Guidance
historyItems.originalSummary: Renaissance Investment Management, an investment management company, released its Q3 2026 investor letter for "Large Cap Growth Strategy." The letter can be downloaded here . Stocks showed modest gains in Q3, with the S&P 500 up 2.3%. Energy, Technology, and Health Care sectors excelled, while Utilities, Industrials, Real Estate, and Consumer Discretionary lagged. Market breadth was narrow, with many stocks remaining significantly below their 52-week highs. The Russell 1000 Growth returned 0.9%, while large-cap stocks outperformed small-cap. Bonds experienced negative returns as 30-year U.S. Treasury yields rose, influenced by fiscal concerns and geopolitical tensions. The Federal Reserve raised interest rates in response to unexpected economic growth and persistent inflation. S&P 500 earnings soared 52% year-over-year, buoyed by selected mark-to-market gains, with future estimates being upgraded. Free cash flow growth has been mixed due to investments in AI and infrastructure, but broader market prospects are improving. Also, check the Fund's top five holdings to see its best picks for 2026.

historyItems.title: 科技巨頭深化人工智慧合作，英偉達和 AMD 將向 Meta 投資 40 億美元
historyItems.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. 今天宣布 Nvidia Corp. 和 Advanced Micro Devices Inc. 計劃購買其價值 40 億美元的股票。
historyItems.originalTitle: Nvidia, AMD to invest $4 billion in Meta as tech giants deepen AI partnership
historyItems.originalSummary: Meta Platforms Inc. today announced that Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. plan to buy $4 billion worth of its shares. The chipmakers will purchase the equity as part of an up to $95 billion stock sale that the Facebook parent intends to kick off in the near future. The fundraising initiative will also include the participation of Broadcom Inc. Meta didn’t specify how much the company is investing, but it stated on Monday that Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom together plan to invest $5 billion. That suggests the networking chip giant will buy $1 billion in shares. Nvidia is investing $3 billion as part of a newly expanded partnership that also includes other components. Notably, Meta plans to broaden its use of the chipmaker’s Rubin graphics processing units and Vera central processing units. Companies often deploy the two chips together in Nvidia-designed DGX Vera Rubin NVL72 appliances. Each system includes 72 GPUs and 36 CPUs. Meta also plans to buy more Nvidia networking gear. It will expand its use of the Spectrum-X Ethernet product family, which includes SuperNICs and switches. SuperNICs are chips that connect servers to a data center’s network, while switches coordinate how traffic flows through that network. GPU clusters’ traffic patterns tend to change rapidly. As a result, connectivity bottlenecks sometimes emerge faster than the network can respond to them. Nvidia says that its Spectrum-X Ethernet product series addresses the challenge by checking GPU traffic for anomalies at sub-microsecond time intervals. A microsecond corresponds to one millionth of a second. Another focus of Meta’s planned network investment is Nvidia’s BlueField-4 chip family. The accelerators in the series are designed to speed common networking, storage and cybersecurity tasks. Nvidia will help Meta improve the performance and cost efficiency of its Muse large language model family. The effort will extend to the Facebook parent’s eponymous consumer AI agent. Additionally, Meta plans to explore “collaboration opportunities” related to Nvidia’s recently introduced OpenShell Reference Architecture. It’s a collection of technical resources that makes it easier to run the chipmaker’s OpenShell toolkit. The toolkit runs AI agents in isolated sandboxes designed to mitigate cybersecurity risks. “Nvidia and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents, so Muse can empower billions of people to achieve more and pursue greater ambitions,” said Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang. AMD, which will invest $1 billion in Meta, today revealed that the Facebook parent has adopted its Helios rack design. Helios contains 72 GPUs much like the DGX Vera Rubin NVL72. It’s based on AMD’s latest Instinct MI450 graphics card architecture, Epyc CPUs and Pensando data processing units, which are the chipmaker’s answer to the BlueField-4.

historyItems.summary: 一年前，「我們應該使用哪種模型？」的答案很簡單：無論哪款前沿模型在本週排行榜上名列前茅。然後開放模型迎頭趕上。它們的成本只是其一小部分，您可以在您想要的地方運行它們，並且您的資料仍然屬於您。很多團隊都做出了轉變。
historyItems.originalTitle: Introducing Cisco Model Foundry: Bringing AI to our partners
historyItems.originalSummary: A year ago, the answer to “which model should we use?” was simple: whichever frontier model topped the leaderboard that week. Then open models caught up. They cost a fraction as much, you could run them where you wanted, and your data stayed yours. Plenty of teams made the switch. Then they pointed those models at real work. An operator reports that R2 lost every route from R1, but ping across the link still works. A security team needs to find the three files in a million-line codebase most likely to hold a vulnerability. An observability team needs to spot the one interface that matters in a week of telemetry. This is where general-purpose models, open or closed, start to struggle. We think the next leap comes from a model that already knows the domain and then learns your customer. That second step runs on your data and your relationships, and it’s where partners lead. Today at Partner Summit, we’re introducing Cisco Model Foundry , a new platform service in Cisco Cloud Control. It gives partners access to Cisco’s purpose-built models and lets them serve those models in customer applications. When the use case calls for it, partners can also fine-tune the models on their customers’ own data, all in one place. Access Cisco’s domain models. Model Foundry opens up the models Cisco has built on four decades of networking, security, and operations knowledge. Several of them previously ran only inside our own products. Browse the catalog, open the Playground, paste in a real problem, and see how each model handles it before you commit. Put them to work. In Model Foundry, you create an API key, set an expiration, choose a model, and you’re connected. The API is OpenAI-compatible, so it plugs into the agents, tools, and workflows you already run. Administrators get tenant-scoped keys, per-model access controls, and full visibility into usage by model, key, and day. Tailor it when it counts. Fine-tuning means taking the knowledge that makes a network or a business unique and training the model on it. It’s built for the large volumes of data that partners and customers already have: configs, log messages, alerts, tickets, and agent traces from thousands of devices. Model Foundry handles the hard parts, from the GPUs to the training pipeline to built-in evaluation that runs the base and tuned models side by side. You see where tuning helped, and where it didn’t, before anything reaches production. Many partners don’t need to fine-tune to get value. A purpose-built Cisco model, served as-is, is built to outperform generic open models on domain work. Fine-tuning is there for the moments when “good” isn’t good enough.

historyItems.originalTitle: Verizon Lifts Outlook, Inks Amazon Deal Worth More Than $2 Billion
historyItems.originalSummary: By Kelly Cloonan Verizon Communications boosted its full-year outlook again as it continues to attract new customers for its postpaid phone service. The mobile carrier also on Monday said it signed a deal valued at more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services to supply dark fiber for agentic and generative artificial-intelligence workloads. The agreement follows a similar deal earlier this year with Alphabet's Google, which was valued at more than $1 billion. "These two contracts are a clear signal that the largest builders of AI infrastructure in the world are choosing Verizon as a strategic connectivity partner," Chief Executive Dan Schulman said during a call with analysts. Schulman said Verizon is in talks with additional hyperscalers, neocloud providers and large enterprise clients to supply fiber connectivity. The company is also seeing momentum with several partners looking to use its network hubs for AI inference and edge computing, he said. Verizon gained a net 406,000 postpaid phone connections in the latest quarter, marking its strongest third-quarter performance on the closely watched metric in five years. Analysts polled by FactSet expected 195,300 postpaid phone net additions. Schulman said the company is gaining loyal, high-value customers as it shifts away from heavy subsidies to focus on other offerings, like its expanded loyalty program and its Simplicity plan, which it rolled out earlier this year. "We are not buying customers. We are winning them on revenue-positive terms and keeping them longer," Schulman said during a call with analysts. The postpaid strength helped Verizon post higher third-quarter profit and revenue. Schulman, who took the helm of Verizon last October, said the latest quarterly results are proof that it's evolved into a structurally different company. "Verizon is in a fundamentally better position operationally, financially and competitively," Schulman said. "Our transformation has taken root and our results show it." The latest results prompted the company to raise its full-year guidance for the third consecutive quarter. Verizon now expects adjusted earnings per share of $5.04 to $5.06 for the full year, compared with its prior view of $4.99 to $5.04, and now projects total full-year postpaid phone net additions of about 1.1 million to 1.2 million, up from a previous range of 875,000 to one million. The company also raised its projection for mobility and broadband service revenue growth to be in the upper half of its prior forecast of 2.5% to 3% for the year. Wall Street projects adjusted earnings of $5 per share and postpaid phone net additions of 975,000 for the year. Verizon's third-quarter profit came in at $5.3 billion, or $1.25 a share, compared with $5.06 billion, or $1.17 a share, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings per share were $1.31, compared with analyst estimates of $1.27. Revenue ticked up 1.5% to $34.3 billion, compared with analyst estimates of $34.77 billion. historyItems.originalTitle: Exclusive: Inside Unusual Machines' $52 Million Drone Battery Acquisition
historyItems.originalSummary: Order Helps Powerus Scale Production of Autonomous and Counter-Drone Systems to Meet Growing Demand ORLANDO, FL / ACCESS Newswire / October 22, 2026 / Unusual Machines, Inc. (NYSE American:UMAC), a leading manufacturer of NDAA-compliant drone components, today announced that it has received a $16.9 million purchase order from Powerus Corporation (Nasdaq:PUSA), a U.S. defense technology company focused on autonomous and unmanned systems. The order covers critical drone components, including motors, batteries, cameras, and video transmitters (VTX), for use across Powerus’s unmanned systems portfolio “The need for effective autonomous and counter-drone systems is growing rapidly, and Powerus is turning that urgency into action,” said Allan Evans, CEO of Unusual Machines. “This latest order builds on our partnership and underscores the importance of a reliable domestic supply chain behind those systems.” The order expands the companies’ commercial relationship as Powerus scales production to meet growing demand. It follows a previous order exceeding $5 million, announced in April 2026, and a $30 million strategic equity investment by Unusual Machines in Powerus, disclosed in June 2026. “The autonomous systems we deliver to our global customers support missions across incredibly complex and evolving operating environments,” said Brett Velicovich, Co-founder and President at Powerus. “Working with Unusual Machines in the U.S. means we can deliver critical products faster and more affordably to our customers, no matter where they are.” Unusual Machines is a leading provider of NDAA-compliant drone components, focused on building a domestic supply chain for the growing U.S. drone industry. The Company manufactures a broad portfolio of critical components, including flight controllers, electronic speed controllers, video systems, motors, FPV headsets, cameras and, following its acquisition of Upgrade Energy, batteries and power systems. Unusual Machines is expanding U.S. manufacturing to meet increasing demand from defense, enterprise, and commercial customers, while serving the consumer FPV market through its Fat Shark and Rotor Riot brands. According to Fact.MR, the U.S. drone components market represents a $3 billion to $5 billion opportunity. For more information, visit unusualmachines.com . Powerus Corporation (formerly Aureus Greenway Holdings Inc., Nasdaq:PUSA) builds and scales unified autonomous systems designed to move, protect, and sustain critical assets in high-risk environments, with capabilities spanning heavy-lift platforms, autonomous air systems, autonomous maritime systems, mission systems, training and support, and U.S.-based manufacturing. Powerus Corporation also owns and manages two golf courses in the Orlando, Florida region. On October 1, 2026, Powerus completed its previously announced merger with AGH; shares continue trading on Nasdaq under the symbol PUSA. Learn more at power.us. Investor: investors@unusualmachines.com Media: media@unusualmachines.com Investor Relations: Santosh Patel ir@power.us 404-314-8141

historyItems.originalSummary: Ariel Investments , an investment management company, released its "Ariel Appreciation Fund" Q3 2026 investor letter. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here . Copy main article 1st para. The Fund faced a challenging third quarter of 2026 as rising interest rates, higher energy prices, persistent inflation, and geopolitical uncertainty weighed on mid-cap equities, despite gains in the broader U.S. market. The Fund's Investor Class returned -3.90%, underperforming the Russell Midcap Value Index, which declined 1.98%, and the Russell Midcap Index, which fell 3.00%. Strong earnings, improved guidance, and better operating performance supported several holdings, while concerns about near-term demand, margins, and execution pressured others. The portfolio also experienced weakness in cruise-related and food-equipment businesses, reflecting softer travel trends, higher fuel costs, inflationary pressures, and investor concerns about near-term profitability. During the quarter, the Fund exited its position in a cruise operator and redeployed the proceeds into another major cruise company, sold an electronic-payments holding, and added exposure to a security, residential technology, and fire-safety distribution business following its spin-off. The Fund also received shares in a newly separated food-processing business. Looking ahead, Ariel expects volatility to persist as inflation, monetary policy, and economic growth remain uncertain. The firm views market dislocations as opportunities to acquire quality businesses trading below intrinsic value, emphasizing durable competitive advantages, strong balance sheets, cash generation, and long-term earnings potential. In addition, please check the Fund's top five holdings to know its best picks in 2026.

historyItems.summary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) 剛剛制定了一項積極的服務準備工作，概述了在 2026 年底之前點亮美國、加拿大、日本、英國和沙烏地阿拉伯的衛星蜂窩覆蓋的計劃。對投資者來說，圍繞 AST SpaceMobile 的故事比服務路線圖更加不穩定。股價較前一交易日下跌5.21%，近一個月下跌39.13%，年初至今下跌53.55%，但三年總股東報酬極高。這表明長期支持者已經獲得了非常大的收益，儘管最近的拋售表明人們對此次推出的執行風險和時機的擔憂日益增加。
historyItems.originalTitle: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) Stock Dropped, So What Is Driving Attention Now?
historyItems.originalSummary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) just laid out an aggressive service readiness push, outlining plans to light up satellite cellular coverage across the United States, Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia before the end of 2026. For investors, the story around AST SpaceMobile has been far more volatile than the service roadmap. The share price has fallen 5.21% over the last session, is down 39.13% over the past month and 53.55% year to date, yet the three year total shareholder return is extremely high. This suggests long term backers have already experienced very large gains even as recent selling points to rising concern about execution risk and timing around this rollout.

historyItems.title: SpaceX 正在洽談接入 80,000 個蜂窩基地台的新網絡
historyItems.summary: Investing.com—彭博新聞社報導，SpaceX 正在討論獲得美國至少 80,000 個蜂窩基地台的接入權，該公司股價週五在美國盤前交易中上漲超過 2%。彭博社報道稱，此舉將標誌著朝著建立第四家全國性無線營運商邁出了具體的一步。據稱，這家衛星巨頭正在與包括 Crown Castle International Corp （NYSE：CCI）在內的主要塔營運商進行談判，以收集補充其軌道網路所需的實體基礎設施。
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX in Talks to Access 80,000 Cell Sites for New Network
historyItems.originalSummary: Investing.com -- SpaceX shares rose by more than 2% in premarket U.S. trading on Friday after Bloomberg News reported that the rocket company is in discussions to secure access to at least 80,000 cell sites across the United States. Bloomberg reported that the move would signal a concrete step toward establishing a fourth nationwide wireless carrier. The satellite giant is said to be negotiating with major tower operators, including Crown Castle International Corp (NYSE:CCI), as it gathers the physical infrastructure required to complement its orbital network. Crown Castle shares surged by more than 7% premarket.

historyItems.originalTitle: Purdue, GlobalFoundries expand partnership with master research agreement
historyItems.originalSummary: WEST LAFAYETTE, Ind. (WLFI) - Purdue University has announced a master research agreement with GlobalFoundries, a manufacturer of essential semiconductors. Purdue says the agreement will significantly expand the university’s research capabilities, and bolster the talent pipeline in the semi-conductor ecosystem. The agreement builds upon a strategic partnership first announced in November 2022. Purdue says it will create a streamlined framework for multiple collaborative projects. Under the unified framework, Purdue says the agreement enables new research initiatives to launch quickly and efficiently, accelerating innovation in semiconductor technology. Since 2023, GlobalFoundries has hosted students from Purdue’s summer training, awareness, and readiness for semiconductors program at its U.S. headquarters.

historyItems.originalSummary: By Katherine Hamilton Deckers Outdoor cut its outlook, citing a highly promotional shoe industry. Shares slid 7% to $79.15 in after-hours trading Thursday. Western Digital's latest earnings report wasn't enough to get the stock back on track after investors sold off AI shares during day trading. Shares were down 5% to $336.50 after the bell. Bloom Energy had a negative cash flow in the latest quarter as it continued to spend heavily. The stock fell 5% to $206.21. historyItems.originalTitle: Nebius secures $3.5 billion financing facility with Citi

historyItems.originalTitle: TTM Technologies Fiscal Q3 non-GAAP Earnings, Revenue Rise; Initiates Fiscal 2027 Preliminary Outlook
historyItems.originalSummary: Interested in TTM Technologies, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better. TTM Technologies delivered record third-quarter results: Revenue rose 60% year over year to $1.2 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share more than doubled to $1.46. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 20.1% from 16.1%, driven by stronger volume, favorable product mix and execution gains. Data Center & Networking led growth, with sales up 115% and accounting for 41% of revenue, as demand increased for higher-value N+M circuit boards. Aerospace and defense also remained strong, with a record $2 billion backlog and a 1.6 book-to-bill ratio. TTM raised its 2026 outlook to $4.47 billion-$4.49 billion in revenue and issued preliminary 2027 guidance of $6.5 billion-$6.75 billion. The company is planning an additional $400 million capacity investment and pursuing acquisitions, including the proposed $650 million purchase of Ophir Optics.

historyItems.originalTitle: What Is Vertiv Holdings Co (VRT) Really Changing With 14 Day AI Factory Builds?
historyItems.originalSummary: Vertiv Holdings Co (NYSE:VRT) and NVIDIA launched a DSX POD modular AI factory reference design that targets 14 day deployment cycles. The DSX POD uses pre engineered power and cooling modules plus advanced virtualization to shorten traditional 6 month AI build timelines. Vertiv is running a multiphase DSX POD implementation in Norway and teaming with Dassault Systèmes to virtually design and validate AI factories. historyItems.originalTitle: LRCX: Record revenue and earnings, with December-quarter guidance for $8.60B revenue
historyItems.originalSummary: Revenue: $8.22 billion, up 22% sequentially and 54% year-over-year; fifth consecutive quarter of record revenue. Gross Margin: Record 52.4%, up from 52% in the June quarter on favorable customer and product mix. Operating Margin: Record 40.2%, up from 38.4% in the June quarter; first time topping 40%. Diluted EPS: Record $2.20; diluted share count ~1.26 billion. Operating Expenses: $1 billion, up from $916 million prior quarter; R&D ~two-thirds of total. Deferred Revenue: $2.66 billion, up $227 million from the June quarter. Memory Systems Revenue: 46% of systems revenue (record dollar level), up 120% year-over-year; NAND 26% of systems revenue (up from 23%), NAND dollars up ~40% sequentially; DRAM 20% of systems revenue (down from 23%), record dollar level. Foundry Systems Revenue: Record; 46% of systems revenue, up from 44% in the June quarter. Logic and Other Systems Revenue: 8% of systems revenue, down from 10% in the June quarter. CSBG Revenue: Fourth consecutive record quarter at nearly $2.5 billion, up slightly sequentially and 40% year-over-year; calendar 2026 growth expected above 30% year-over-year, with over 15% growth expected in calendar 2027.

historyItems.originalSummary: Sundar Pichai just confirmed Google Cloud is turning away customers, and he called the reason behind it non-negotiable. historyItems.originalTitle: Nokia advances AI-RAN toward commercial deployment and physical AI, launches sovereign agentic AI platform for telco autonomy with NVIDIA
historyItems.originalSummary: Nokia advances AI-RAN toward commercial deployment and physical AI, launches sovereign agentic AI platform for telco autonomy with NVIDIA Berlin, Germany – Nokia today announced the next step in how it is bringing AI-native networks to commercial reality with NVIDIA, with new capabilities that apply AI within radio processing, support intelligence close to where data is generated and extend governed AI agents for cross-domain network operations. Building on the industry’s first commercial AI-RAN platform, announced in July, AI-RAN is being integrated into live networks and moving closer to deployment. Together, Nokia and NVIDIA are creating the real-time network foundation needed for physical-AI applications while giving operators a practical path to improve today’s 5G and 5G Advanced networks and evolve to AI-native 6G. Customer progress moves AI-RAN closer to deployment One year ago, Nokia and NVIDIA formed a partnership to add NVIDIA-powered, commercial-grade AI-RAN products to Nokia’s radio access network portfolio. The companies are now applying AI within the 5G signal-processing chain, including channel estimation, beamforming, multi-user MIMO pairing and scheduling. Nokia AI-native anyRAN software, running on NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer, provides a software-defined foundation for integrating AI-powered radio functions that improve network capacity and performance.

historyItems.summary: 現在，馬斯克 (Elon Musk) 應該回歸 SpaceX (SPCX) 的創始人模式，轉向他非常擅長的其他事情：迷人的、富有遠見的創始人，正在向那些想要進入馬斯克宇宙的人索要大筆資金。因為從馬斯克在周二晚間財報電話會議上的評論來看，他將需要大量新資本來實現 Terrafab、Starlink 寬頻和火箭可重複使用性的積極增長時間表。也許比大多數投資人想像的多很多。
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX earnings left one big question unanswered
historyItems.originalSummary: The moment is now for Elon Musk to dial back founder mode at SpaceX ( SPCX ) and dial back up something else he is very good at: charming visionary founder who is asking for large sums of capital from people who want entry to the Muskverse. Because judging by Musk's commentary on his late Tuesday earnings call, he will need a lot of fresh capital to deliver on aggressive growth timelines for Terrafab, Starlink broadband and rocket reusability. Perhaps way more than most investors think.

historyItems.summary: 馬斯克 (Elon Musk) 花了數年時間將特斯拉和 SpaceX 打造成兩個價值數萬億美元的科技帝國。現在，他正在考慮讓他們在一起。週二被問及合併是否是一個好主意時，馬斯克明確表示：「是的。」前景不僅僅是假設。馬斯克表示，已經成立了特別委員會來評估潛在的交易，但他強調，不能保證合併一定會發生，也沒有達成任何協議。
historyItems.originalTitle: Why Elon Musk Wants to Merge SpaceX and Tesla
historyItems.originalSummary: Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires. Now, he is considering bringing them together . Asked on Tuesday whether a merger would be a good idea, Musk was clear: "Yes." The prospect is more than hypothetical. Musk said special committees have been formed to assess a potential deal, although he stressed that there is no guarantee a merger will happen and that nothing has been agreed.

historyItems.summary: 伊隆馬斯克在周二的第三季財報電話會議上表示，特斯拉和 SpaceX 已經成立了特別委員會來討論可能的合併。擔任兩家公司執行長的馬斯克表示，特別委員會是應股東的要求成立的，由獨立董事組成（儘管他沒有透露姓名）。他還指出，他不是這兩個委員會的成員，也沒有參與任何討論。 「因為我是一個衝突方，所以我實際上無法參與特別委員會的討論，」馬斯克說。
historyItems.originalTitle: A possible SpaceX-Tesla merger? Here's what people are saying
historyItems.originalSummary: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter’s third quarter earnings call Tuesday. Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of independent directors (though he did not name them). He also noted that he is not a member of either committee, nor involved in any of the discussions. “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees,” Musk said. “So it’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I can’t be in the conversation.” The groups have not reached agreement on the terms of any transaction — and there’s no guarantee that they will. “At the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this,” he continued. “And particularly on the Tesla side, we will need a 50 percent vote of all shares, not just those who vote, but of all shareholders. And that’s quite a high hurdle to try to achieve.” That said, Musk called the possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX merger a “good idea.” He continued: > I do think there’s a lot of merit to combining companies as we are pretty much in the superintelligence singularity. And there’s a lot to be gained from cooperating on developing superintelligence software, chip design, the TeraFab, obviously robotics, mass to orbit with the Starmind constellation, connectivity. So I think it would be a good idea, but it’s really up to the special committees of both companies. They’ve got to come up with something and then that’s going to be put to the shareholders as a vote. A Tesla-SpaceX merger would be a blockbuster corporate deal creating a mega-entity valued upwards of $3.6 trillion. But combining Musk’s car and energy company with his AI and rocket company would not be without its tradeoffs. A lot depends on which company absorbs the other. To buy SpaceX, Tesla would have to create millions of new stock shares, which for current Tesla owners would mean owning a smaller slice of a much larger pie. SpaceX’s launch goals require tens of billions of dollars every year — extra spending that could drain Tesla’s ability to build new car factories and battery plants. That said, most Wall Street analysts and legal experts believe SpaceX would acquire Tesla (or absorb it through a stock swap) rather than vice versa. Since its IPO, SpaceX has maintained a higher valuation than Tesla. A merger in that direction would allow SpaceX shareholders to hold the majority control of the combined mega-entity. Some Tesla shareholders may balk at this deal. But it would also create one company for those who believe in Musk’s vision of the future — robot cars, humanoid robots, AI super-intelligence, and human habitats on Mars — in which to place their investments. And Tesla shareholder approved Musk’s enormous pay package last year — even after a Delaware judge tossed it over lack of independence. Earlier this month, Barclays published a client note suggesting a potential Tesla-SpaceX combination could be announced ahead of Tesla’s annual shareholder meeting scheduled for December 3, 2026.
